$comment: The showcase spine. Every consumer reads this file: the rehearsal script, the mission-control fallback, the presenter guide, and the repository tests. Change the sequence here and nowhere else.
title: GitHub Beyond Coding: The Agentic Engineering Loop

shape.slideLayout: 3 section dividers + 11 scene presentation cards + 1 closing takeaway
shape.sentence: A nine-stage engineering loop shown in eleven demo scenes; only one lifecycle stage is coding.
shape.note: The return to the next signal is the arrow back to stage one, not a tenth stage. Scenes are how the hour is presented; stages are what the loop is made of. Never conflate the two counts.
questions: Who is accountable for the merge?
primitives: Durable, assignable work items an agent can read where the code lives
A reviewable change set with line-level discussion
Deterministic checks bound to that change set
Branch rules expressed as reviewable configuration
Required review by named owners, attributed to a person
Environment approval, federated credentials, build provenance
A path for production signal to become the next work item

stageMapping.$comment: Every scene declares which lifecycle stage it puts on the screen. A scene marked crossCutting frames the loop rather than demonstrating one stage of it, and does not count towards coverage: each of the nine canonical stages must be demonstrated by at least one scene that is not cross-cutting. sceneMarker is what the card subtitle and the presenter crosswalk both render, so the two can never drift.

scenes.tabRouting: Stay on tab 1 for the whole scene.
scenes.title: Nine stages carry one change, and only one is coding
scenes.expectedState: The nine-stage loop with the seven questions and their primitives beneath it, so the room can audit its own stack while listening.
scenes.stopCondition: If the deck will not enter slides mode, present the article view and continue.
scenes.sceneMarker: All nine stages · Q1 to Q7

scenes.tabRouting: Open tab 3 first for the finished issue, then tab 2 for the source and the run.
scenes.title: Reasoning proposes one issue; a compiled contract bounds the write
scenes.expectedState: The finished issue on screen within fifteen seconds, then the pipeline and the bounded control contract in the frontmatter. A fresh run is triggered into the background only.
scenes.stopCondition: Show the finished issue first, always. Never make the room watch a queue.

trustModel.note: The input is committed synthetic telemetry: reviewed repository content, not attacker-controlled. The control that matters here is the bounded, code-reviewable contract in the frontmatter, not an input gate.

scenes.tabRouting: Stay on tab 3; scroll to the intake comment.
scenes.title: Contracts outlive engines, and this one already proved it
scenes.expectedState: Prepared output: one comment with four headings and at most three allowlisted labels, beside the engine-churn point.
scenes.stopCondition: Three minutes, hard. Prepared only: the OpenCode lock reports the firewall disabled and maps the Copilot token into the model sandbox. Never run this lane live.

trustModel.note: Issue text is attacker-controlled. This lane is the one that needs the label and actor gate, and it has one; the pulse lane does not need it because its input is committed content.

scenes.title: Ten acceptance criteria, ten named tests, checked both ways
scenes.expectedState: SPEC-001 open beside the acceptance mapping table.
scenes.stopCondition: None. This scene is repository content and cannot fail.
scenes.sceneMarker: Stage 3 Contract · Q1 and Q2 of 7

scenes.tabRouting: First backwards jump: return to tab 1.
scenes.title: Four execution surfaces, one repository contract
scenes.expectedState: The four surfaces on screen: IDE, CLI, purpose-built agent app, GitHub-hosted cloud agents. No tool is opened live.

scenes.title: A good agent pull request is small enough to read in the room
scenes.expectedState: Prepared agent session and its pull request, opened on the diff.
scenes.stopCondition: Never start a fresh delegation live.

scenes.title: Eight checks, one ruleset, one accountable human
scenes.expectedState: All eight deterministic checks, the ruleset and CODEOWNERS requirement, and the attributed approval, all visible on one slide.
scenes.stopCondition: If a check is still running after three minutes, switch to the prepared evidence artefact.

fallback.label: Prepared checks, review, and authority state

scenes.title: Merging is a code decision; deploying is an authority decision
scenes.expectedState: The provenance record with its mode field, the environment approval gate, and the federated identity.
scenes.stopCondition: Attestation needs an entitled repository. If unavailable, show the simulated record and say so out loud.

scenes.tabRouting: Second backwards jump: return to tab 1 and stay there to the end.
scenes.title: Production signal correlated to source under an identity scoped to one workload
scenes.expectedState: The cloud-neutral pattern stated first, then the Azure implementation as one concrete proof, then the stated limitation.
scenes.stopCondition: Never open a live cloud portal. This scene is cited evidence from a public repository.

scenes.title: Keep Bitbucket and Jira; pilot one repository for two weeks
scenes.expectedState: Bitbucket and Jira coexistence, the three cost lines, the two phases, the three dispositions, the pilot participants, the five artefacts and the day-14 decision, all visible.
scenes.stopCondition: None. This is the commercial ask and it is never cut.
